summary: The TAILOR Act of 2025 requires federal financial regulatory agencies to tailor their rules and regulations to limit the burden on financial institutions, taking into account their risk profiles and business models. The bill applies to future regulations and certain rules adopted over the previous 15 years, mandates reports to Congress on tailoring actions and modernizing bank supervision, and reduces reporting requirements for certain community banks.

affected_groups.effect: Must tailor regulatory actions to risk profiles and business models, document compliance in rulemakings, review past rules, and submit multiple reports to Congress.
Receive reduced reporting requirements for their first and third report of condition each year.
affected_groups.group: Community banks eligible for the Community Bank Leverage Ratio

key_provisions: Federal financial regulatory agencies must consider the risk profile and business model of institutions when creating new regulations and limit regulatory impact and burdens.
Agencies must disclose and document in proposed and final rulemakings how they applied these tailoring requirements.
Agencies must submit annual reports to Congress regarding specific tailoring actions taken.
Agencies must review final regulations issued within the 15 years prior to the bill's introduction, apply the tailoring requirements to them, and make any revisions within 3 years.
Federal banking agencies must establish reduced reporting requirements for all banks eligible for the Community Bank Leverage Ratio for their first and third condition reports of the year.
Federal banking agencies must report to Congress within 18 months on the modernization of bank supervision, including workforce training, changing business models, and necessary statutory changes.
missing_information: Specific numerical estimates of cost savings or exact numbers of affected institutions.
Details on what specific metrics will define reduced reporting requirements outside of referencing existing statutory criteria.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The TAILOR Act of 2025 requires federal financial regulatory agencies to tailor their rules and regulations to limit the burden on financial institutions, taking into account their risk profiles and business models. The bill applies to future regulations and certain rules adopted over the previous 15 years, mandates reports to Congress on tailoring actions and modernizing bank supervision, and reduces reporting requirements for certain community banks.
summary_detail.significance: The bill's significance is evaluated as moderate because it mandates widespread administrative and procedural changes across multiple federal financial regulatory agencies, alters reporting requirements for community banks, and requires a look-back review of rules adopted over a 15-year period. Its score is 60 because, while it affects rulemaking and reporting structures across the federal financial regulatory system, it directs procedural adjustments rather than rewriting major underlying financial statutes. Evidence: "Each Federal financial institutions regulatory agency shall conduct a review of all final regulations issued pursuant to statutes enacted during the period beginning on the date that is 15 years before the date on which this Act is introduced."
